status_help: drilling it alone or in low-stakes settings
did it in a real conversation, meeting or talk at least once
level_notes: Ordered the way speaking coaches and Toastmasters build it: voice first, then the habits that show up in every conversation, then prepared talks, then thinking on your feet, then presence. Two rules that hold at every level — record yourself, and practise out loud, not in your head.

skills.name: Diaphragmatic breathing for speech
skills.how: Breathe low into the belly, then speak on the exhale. Low breath = steady voice and slower nerves.
skills.practice: Hand on the belly, 4-count in, speak a sentence on the out-breath. 3 min a day.
skills.signal: You can finish a long sentence without running out of air or rushing.

skills.name: Vocal warm-up (hum, lip trills, sirens)
skills.how: Two minutes of humming, lip trills and pitch slides before anything that matters.
skills.practice: In the car or shower before a meeting.
skills.signal: Voice feels 'forward' and doesn't crack on the first sentence.

skills.name: Articulation & tongue twisters
skills.how: Over-enunciate consonants; run tongue twisters slowly then fast.
skills.practice: One twister, five times, daily — 'red leather, yellow leather'.
skills.signal: People stop asking you to repeat yourself.

skills.name: Record yourself and review
skills.how: Phone camera, 60 seconds on any topic. Watch once for content, once for voice, once with sound off for body.
skills.practice: Weekly. Keep the clips — the progress is the motivation.
skills.signal: Watching yourself stops being painful and starts being useful.
skills.note: The single highest-leverage habit on this board.

skills.name: The HAIL foundation (Julian Treasure)
skills.how: Honesty, Authenticity, Integrity, Love — plus the seven sins to drop. The 10-minute talk that frames everything else here.
skills.practice: Watch once; notice one 'sin' in your own speech this week.
skills.signal: You can name your own default habit.

skills.name: Filler words → silence
skills.how: Replace um/like/so with a pause. Fillers are the mouth buying time; give it time instead.
skills.practice: Count fillers in your recording; then re-record the same minute with pauses.
skills.signal: Under 2 fillers a minute in a recording.

skills.name: Pace & the deliberate pause
skills.how: Aim for ~150 words a minute; pause a full beat after the important sentence.
skills.practice: Read a paragraph aloud with a timer; insert pauses at every full stop.
skills.signal: Pauses feel long to you and normal to listeners.

skills.name: Concise: the 3-2-1 / headline-first habit
skills.how: Say the conclusion first, then at most three supports. Stop.
skills.practice: Answer any question in one sentence before you explain.
skills.signal: People stop interrupting to redirect you.

skills.name: Ending sentences down (uptalk & vocal fry)
skills.how: Statements land on a falling pitch; rising pitch is for questions. Keep breath behind the last word so it doesn't crackle.
skills.practice: Record ten statements; mark which ones rise.
skills.signal: Your statements sound like decisions.
skills.yt_by: Tarle Speech · fix vocal fry & upspeak

skills.name: Active listening
skills.how: Listen to understand, reflect back what you heard, ask one follow-up before responding.
skills.practice: In one conversation a day, paraphrase before you reply.
skills.signal: People say 'exactly' to you more often.

skills.name: PREP structure (Point · Reason · Example · Point)
skills.how: The all-purpose skeleton for an answer, an update or a two-minute talk.
skills.practice: Take any opinion you hold and say it in PREP form, timed to 60 s.
skills.signal: You can structure an answer while the question is still being asked.

skills.name: Openings that hook
skills.how: Question, story, startling fact, or a bold statement — never 'today I'm going to talk about'.
skills.practice: Write three openings for the same talk; test them on a friend.
skills.signal: The room goes quiet in your first ten seconds.

skills.name: Storytelling structure
skills.how: Situation → struggle → change → point. One story per key idea.
skills.practice: Tell one 90-second personal story with a clear turning point.
skills.signal: People retell your story back to you.

skills.name: Closing & call to action
skills.how: Return to the opening, one-sentence summary, one specific ask. Never end on 'so… yeah, that's it'.
skills.practice: Script your last two sentences word for word.
skills.signal: You know your last line before you start.

skills.name: Presenting slides without reading them
skills.how: Slides carry the picture; you carry the words. One idea per slide, glance and turn back to the room.
skills.practice: Present a deck with the screen off once.
skills.signal: You could give the talk if the projector died.

skills.name: Vocal variety (pitch, volume, emphasis)
skills.how: Change something every sentence: louder, softer, slower, a stressed word.
skills.practice: Read a children's book aloud as if to a child.
skills.signal: Recordings of you are not monotone at 2× speed.

skills.name: Body language, gestures, eye contact
skills.how: Plant the feet, open hands at waist height, hold eye contact for one full thought per person.
skills.practice: Watch your recording with the sound off.
skills.signal: You forget about your hands.

skills.name: Projection & authority
skills.how: Volume from the breath, not the throat; lower resonance; land the ends of sentences.
skills.practice: Speak to the far wall of an empty room for 2 minutes.
skills.signal: You're heard at the back without a mic and without shouting.
skills.yt_by: Project your voice to convey authority

skills.name: Managing nerves
skills.how: Reframe 'I'm nervous' as 'I'm excited', greet the audience beforehand, breathe low, move at the start.
skills.practice: Pick one technique and use it before every talk for a month.
skills.signal: Nerves peak before, not during.

skills.name: Give a toast or short occasion speech
skills.how: Name the person, one story, one wish, raise the glass. Under 90 seconds.
skills.practice: Prepare one for the next birthday before you're asked.
skills.signal: You volunteer.

skills.name: Impromptu speaking (table topics)
skills.how: Pause, pick a structure (PREP, past–present–future, pro–con), answer for 1–2 minutes, land it.
skills.practice: Random-question generator, 2 minutes, recorded, 3× a week.
skills.signal: The pause before you answer feels like power, not panic.
skills.yt_by: Think on your feet · table topics

skills.name: Handling Q&A and tough questions
skills.how: Listen fully, repeat or reframe the question, answer briefly, check back. 'I don't know, I'll find out' is an answer.
skills.practice: Have a friend fire hostile questions at a talk you know.
skills.signal: Q&A is your favourite part.

skills.name: Speaking up when put on the spot
skills.how: Buy two seconds ('Good question — here's where I land'), headline, one reason, stop.
skills.practice: Volunteer first in one meeting a week.
skills.signal: Being called on stops spiking your heart rate.

skills.name: Small talk & starting conversations
skills.how: Comment on the shared situation, ask an open question, listen for the thread, follow it.
skills.practice: One conversation with a stranger a week.
skills.signal: Silences stop feeling like failures.

skills.name: Being heard in meetings
skills.how: Speak in the first ten minutes, headline first, build on others by name.
skills.practice: Prepare one point before every meeting and say it.
skills.signal: People ask what you think.
skills.yt_by: Get your voice heard in meetings

skills.name: Giving feedback (SBI) & hard conversations
skills.how: Situation → Behaviour → Impact, then ask. Facts before feelings, one issue at a time.
skills.practice: Script the first two sentences of the next hard conversation.
skills.signal: You give the feedback within a day instead of a month.

skills.name: Presenting without notes (memory palace)
skills.how: Turn the talk into 5–7 images placed along a familiar route; walk the route as you speak.
skills.practice: Memorise a 5-minute talk this way once.
skills.signal: You look at the audience the whole time.
